此工作流程旨在比较 JoyAI-Image 单图像编辑与 Qwen Image Edit 2511。其主要目的是帮助创作者测试不同的图像编辑路线如何处理相同或相似的视觉编辑任务，特别是当目标不仅是更改图像，而且还要保留身份、结构、光照、纹理和最终视觉质量时。

该工作流程包含 JoyAI-Image 编辑分支和 Qwen Image Edit 2511 比较分支。 JoyAI分支使用JoyAI-Image-Und-merger_bf16作为视觉理解/CLIP路线，joy_image_transformer作为主要图像转换器，Wan2.1_VAE.pth作为VAE，JoyAI_Image_ENCODER用于图像和提示调节，JoyAI_Image_LATENTS用于潜在准备，JoyAI_Image_SM_KSampler用于采样，JoyAI_Vae_Decoder用于最终解码。该路线侧重于直接单图像指令编辑：上传一张图像，编写编辑命令，然后让模型变换图像，同时保留重要的视觉标识。

Qwen 2511 分支使用 qwen_image_edit_2511_bf16 和 Qwen Image Edit 2511 Lightning 4-step LoRA、qwen_2.5_vl_7b_fp8_scaled 作为视觉语言编码器、qwen_image_vae、TextEncodeQwenImageEditPlus、参考潜在方法节点、KSampler 和平铺 VAE 解码。该分支可用于比较 Qwen 2511 在轻量级加速设置下如何处理细节、光照、身份保留、参考图像理解和速度。

该工作流程对于想要回答实际编辑问题的创作者特别有用：哪种路线可以更好地保留原始角色身份？哪一个更直接地遵循文本指令？哪一个改变背景更自然？哪一种可以产生更好的照明和阴影集成？批量测试哪一个更快？哪一个更适合 Civitai 预览图像、RunningHub 演示、社交媒体封面或本地制作？

JoyAI 的示例聚焦于一个蓝发网络机械女孩被转移到明亮的草原场景，同时保留她的面部特征、双马尾发型、机械耳装置、颈部结构和金属身体。提示还要求真实的户外照明、草原氛围、自然阴影、金属高光以及减少抠图感。这使得它成为身份保存和场景替换的有力考验。

Qwen 2511方面包括人像式光影增强方向，要求面部纹理更清晰、光照更丰富、皮肤细节真实、影棚式人像画质、主体分离度更强。这使得它适合测试 Qwen 2511 在摄影细化、照明增强和受控图像抛光方面是否表现更好。

对于想要在一次编辑实验中比较 JoyAI-Image 和 Qwen Image Edit 2511 的创作者来说，此工作流程是理想的选择。如果您想了解这两种编辑路线在真实工作流程条件下的表现，请观看上面 YouTube 链接的完整教程。

o.en:
This workflow is designed for comparing JoyAI-Image single-image editing with Qwen Image Edit 2511. Its main purpose is to help creators test how different image-editing routes handle the same or similar visual editing task, especially when the goal is not only to change an image, but also to preserve identity, structure, lighting, texture, and final visual quality.

The workflow contains a JoyAI-Image editing branch and a Qwen Image Edit 2511 comparison branch. The JoyAI branch uses JoyAI-Image-Und-merger_bf16 as the visual understanding / CLIP route, joy_image_transformer as the main image transformer, Wan2.1_VAE.pth as the VAE, JoyAI_Image_ENCODER for image-and-prompt conditioning, JoyAI_Image_LATENTS for latent preparation, JoyAI_Image_SM_KSampler for sampling, and JoyAI_Vae_Decoder for final decoding. This route is focused on direct single-image instruction editing: upload one image, write the edit command, and let the model transform the image while keeping the important visual identity.

The Qwen 2511 branch uses qwen_image_edit_2511_bf16 with Qwen Image Edit 2511 Lightning 4-step LoRA, qwen_2.5_vl_7b_fp8_scaled as the visual-language encoder, qwen_image_vae, TextEncodeQwenImageEditPlus, reference-latent method nodes, KSampler, and tiled VAE decoding. This branch is useful for comparing how Qwen 2511 handles detail, lighting, identity retention, reference-image understanding, and speed under a lightweight accelerated setup.

The workflow is especially useful for creators who want to answer practical editing questions: Which route keeps the original character identity better? Which one follows text instructions more directly? Which one changes the background more naturally? Which one produces better lighting and shadow integration? Which one is faster for batch testing? Which one is better for Civitai preview images, RunningHub demos, social media covers, or local production?

The JoyAI example focuses on a blue-haired cyber mechanical girl being transferred into a bright grassland scene while preserving her facial features, twin-tail hairstyle, mechanical ear devices, neck structure, and metallic body. The prompt also asks for realistic outdoor lighting, grassland atmosphere, natural shadows, metal highlights, and reduced cutout feeling. This makes it a strong test for identity preservation and scene replacement.

The Qwen 2511 side includes a portrait-style light-and-shadow enhancement direction, asking for clearer facial texture, richer lighting, realistic skin detail, studio-style portrait quality, and stronger subject separation. This makes it suitable for testing whether Qwen 2511 performs better at photographic refinement, lighting enhancement, and controlled image polishing.

This workflow is ideal for creators who want to compare JoyAI-Image and Qwen Image Edit 2511 in one editing experiment. If you want to see how the two editing routes behave under real workflow conditions, watch the full tutorial from the YouTube link above.
